title: Sales Enablement Prospect Playbook — Positioning, Pricing, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: A single, concise prospect-facing playbook for Redwood Inference sellers and solutions engineers. Includes elevator pitches, core positioning and messaging, competitive talking points, recommended pitch-deck structure, pricing guidance, two short customer case studies, and a security & compliance FAQ for prospect conversations. Use this doc when preparing demos, proposals, and executive briefings.

Audience: SDRs, AEs, Sales Engineers, Partner Account Execs, and Customer Success for early-stage onboarding.

1) Positioning & Messaging

Elevator pitch (30s):
Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLMs predictable and economical in production — low latency, low cost, and portable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We help engineering teams ship LLM features with industry-grade reliability, transparent performance, and control over inference economics.

Core messages (1-2 minute version):
- Production-first: We optimize for real application constraints — throughput, latency SLOs, and cost per token — not just raw model benchmarks.
- Unified runtime across environments: Same API and tooling for Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
- Cost control: Intelligent batching, prefix/KV caching, and model/quantization recommendations that reduce per-token costs without surprising quality regressions.
- Reliability & graceful degradation: Smart routing and fallbacks (model variants, regions, tiers) keep apps online during capacity or regional problems.
- Developer experience: Simple REST/SDK, transparent performance profiles, streaming, tool-calls and eval integrations for safe rollouts.

Top proof points customers care about:
- Multi-hour production latency SLOs across 99th percentile at single-digit hundreds of ms (example configs available).
- Measurable cost savings: Customers typically see 20–60% unit-cost reduction vs naive self-hosting thanks to batching, caching, and model recommendations.
- Enterprise-ready: KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging, and VPC/private control planes for regulated workloads.

2) Target personas & use cases

Primary personas:
- ML/Infra Engineers: Need predictable throughput for model endpoints and controls for quantization and batching.
- Product Engineers (feature owners): Want low-latency, stable user experience and a simple API to iterate.
- Platform/Cloud Architects: Need deployment options and compliance controls for enterprise procurement.

Common use cases:
- Chat assistants (SaaS product features, internal LLM copilots)
- Summarization and document Q&A at scale
- Embeddings & semantic search for knowledge retrieval
- Reranking and multi-model orchestration for precision-sensitive workflows

3) Competitive Brief (short tactical guide)

Primary competitors to call out: Managed LLM APIs (generalist providers), Cloud-managed endpoints (cloud vendor hosted models), Self-hosted inference runtimes.

Competitive matrix (how to frame differences):
- Redwood vs Managed-LLM APIs: Emphasize cost transparency, dedicated capacity options, and production-first tooling (rollouts, tracing). Managed APIs may be easier to start with but lack reserved capacity and private deployment parity.
- Redwood vs Cloud Endpoints: Cloud vendors offer infrastructure breadth; Redwood offers inference-specific runtime optimizations (continuous batching, KV cache management) and a consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private.
- Redwood vs Self-hosted Runtimes: Self-hosting can be cheaper at scale but requires heavy engineering investment. Redwood reduces operational burden, provides performance tuning, SLOs, and built-in fallbacks.

Battlecard — Objections and responses:
- Objection: "We can self-host and save money."
  Response: "Self-hosting requires ongoing optimization (kernel selection, batching, cache management) and hidden costs in ops time. Our customers typically recover the platform premium via 20–60% lower per-request costs and faster feature velocity. We also offer Dedicated/Private options to align unit economics with long-term commitments."
- Objection: "We need full control for compliance."
  Response: "Redwood Private provides a customer-controlled VPC/private control plane and on-prem options. We integrate with KMS/HSM, provide audit logs, and follow enterprise-grade security practices — we can walk through an architecture review."
- Objection: "Vendor lock-in concerns."
  Response: "We support model portability and clear export policies. You can pin model versions and move between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments without rewriting your client code."

4) Recommended pitch deck structure (6–12 slides)

1. Title + hook (business outcome)
2. Problem: Latency, cost, operations complexity of serving LLMs in production
3. Solution overview: Redwood platform + deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private)
4. Architecture diagram: request flow, smart routing, KV cache, fallback policies
5. Performance & cost evidence: per-token cost examples, 99p latency SLOs, benchmark summary
6. Security & compliance: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logging, SOC/ISO evidence (link to security pages)
7. Case study (customer outcome with metrics)
8. Pricing & packaging: sample tiers and buying guidance
9. Rollout plan & timelines: POC -> pilot -> production scales, responsibilities
10. Next steps & ask (technical deep-dive, trial, contractual steps)

Guidance for SE demos:
- Start with a short smoke-test on customer data (or synthetic sample) that demonstrates 99p latency and streaming output.
- Show cost telemetry in Console: token-level breakdown, per-route dashboards, and quality monitoring.
- Demonstrate a canary roll-out and automatic fallback in the console.

5) Pricing guidance (sell-side guidance, not public pricing)

Pricing models we offer (talk track):
- Hosted (usage-based): ideal for evaluation and early production. Price components: per-1K input tokens, per-1K output tokens, embedding unit pricing. Optional add-ons: increased retention, advanced observability.
- Dedicated (committed reserved capacity): monthly/annual committed GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit costs. Includes baseline throughput and burst options.
- Private (enterprise license + deployment): platform fee + support tier; deployment/scoping fees for on-prem.

Suggested anchor tiers for discussions (example figures for negotiation only):
- POC / early stage: low-minimum hosted credits + standard per-token rates
- Growth: committed Dedicated pool (monthly commit) with 15–30% unit discount vs hosted list
- Enterprise: annual Private agreement with deeper discounts, advanced support and SLAs

Discount levers (for AEs):
- Volume commitments (monthly/annual)
- Multi-year contracts
- Bundled observability / retention add-ons
- Professional services (onboarding/architecture review) as separate line items

Price objections: emphasize bill-of-materials approach (tokens, embeddings, retention) and the ROI from reduced ops headcount and faster time-to-feature. Bring finance for deal-specific TCO analysis.

6) Case studies (two short examples for prospect conversations)

Case Study A — SaaS support assistant (mid-market vendor)
- Challenge: High-latency knowledge-base answers and spiky traffic during product releases.
- What we delivered: Dedicated pool with autoscale, KV-prefix caching for common queries, and a canary rollout with automated fallback to a smaller model during peaks.
- Outcome: 95th->99th percentile latency improved from 2.1s to 420ms; average per-request cost dropped 34% after batching and caching. Time-to-market for the feature decreased from 8 weeks to 3 weeks.

Case Study B — Financial services summary engine (regulated workload)
- Challenge: Need on-prem deployment for data residency, strict audit logging, and key management.
- What we delivered: Private deployment in customer VPC, KMS integration, and extended audit retention.
- Outcome: Compliance sign-off in 6 weeks; end-to-end summary latency within SLAs (700ms 99p). Estimated ops time saved: ~0.5 FTE monthly compared to customer’s prior self-hosted approach.

7) Security & Compliance FAQ for prospects (concise answers)

Q: Can customer data leave our network?
A: For Private deployments and VPC modes, customer data stays in your environment. For Hosted, we offer strict tenancy and encryption-in-transit and at-rest; customers with data-residency needs should evaluate Private/Dedicated.

Q: What key management options do you support?
A: We support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can integrate with customer HSMs for Private deployments.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and retention controls?
A: Yes. We provide detailed request/response audit logging, configurable retention windows, and secure export for SIEM. Retention tiers are an add-on.

Q: What certifications and evidence do you have?
A: We publish our compliance posture and evidence packages to the Security & Compliance space. We are actively maintaining SOC/ISO readiness and can share redacted reports under NDA.

Q: How do you handle model safety, toxic output, and hallucinations?
A: We offer tool-calling and structured output policies, content filters, deterministic reranking, and quality-monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals. Evals surface regressions and alert on quality drops during rollouts.

Q: What SLAs are available?
A: Hosted customers get best-effort SLAs; Dedicated customers can purchase SLA-backed throughput and uptime guarantees as part of their contract. Private deployments have contractual uptime and support options per enterprise agreement.

Q: How do you handle incident response and forensics?
A: We provide incident postmortems for platform incidents. For Private deployments, customers maintain their own incident response with support from Redwood. We offer runbooks and engagement during incident handling.

8) Operational checklist for pilots (recommended steps)

- Pre-sales readiness: collect expected qps, typical sequence lengths, expected traffic pattern, and compliance constraints.
- POC: 2–4 week pilot; run synthetic load and 1–2 key production prompts; collect Console metrics and quality baselines.
- Pilot to production: finalize commit level (if Dedicated), sign off on security architecture (if Private), validate canary plan and rollback thresholds.
- Post-launch: monitor per-route SLOs, configure quality alerts tied to evals, and schedule monthly cost-review with engineering.
